title: AI Datasets
answer: Training and evaluation datasets with size, licence, provenance, language coverage, and documented bias.

reading.body:
The datasets layer of AI is documented here mainly through its legal and provenance questions, not its contents: licensing and provenance carries 17 entries against 8 for training corpora and 9 for evaluation sets.

That split is the useful signal. The smallest body of documented material is the training data itself, the corpora that determine what a model can do. The largest is the question of what may lawfully be used and how that can be established. Evaluation sets sit in between, and the framing around them is about what each benchmark actually measures rather than what it scores.

For AI specifically, this ordering matters because data is the input that compute consumes. A model's capability is bounded by the corpus behind it, and the corpus is bounded by what can be licensed and traced. When the provenance record is thicker than the corpus record, the constraint on scaling is not the availability of text or images but the ability to demonstrate where they came from.

The data does not say how large any dataset is, what languages it covers, or what bias has been documented, despite those being named as the subject. It gives counts of entries by category and nothing about their contents. Nothing here speaks to compute, buildings, or power at all, and it should not be read as doing so.
